Workplaces
Workplace First Aid, CPR & AED
OFFICE / WORKSITE
Office staff, shop teams and designated responders who need a shared plan when someone gets hurt or collapses.
HSI or AHA First Aid/CPR/AED is a useful starting point when the employer accepts the specific course and hands-on format.
Federal OSHA general-industry first-aid requirements depend in part on access to nearby medical care; OSHA does not endorse course brands.
Bring a floor plan showing how responders reach each occupied area on each shift.
Does every employee need the same course?
Not necessarily. Start with the roles named in your emergency plan and confirm employer requirements before training.

Manufacturing First Aid, CPR & AED

Identify when first and second shifts overlap and how a coworker can guide EMS through the gate.
Can one class cover both shifts?

Warehouse First Aid, CPR & AED
WAREHOUSE / LOADING DOCK
Distribution teams managing lift traffic, separate loading docks and long distances across the building.
First Aid/CPR/AED for floor and dock responders is usually more relevant than clinical BLS.

Tell us where AEDs are mounted and who can open a dock or gate for EMS after hours.
Can we practice a dock emergency?
Tell us the layout and who normally coordinates the response. Keep any exercises away from operating vehicles and active loading areas.

Construction & trades
Construction Site First Aid, CPR & AED
CONSTRUCTION / TRADES
General contractors, subcontractors and field crews working on changing jobsites.
Discuss an in-person First Aid/CPR/AED course for designated responders, matched to the project’s documentation requirements.

OSHA's construction rule calls for a trained first-aid person available at the worksite when medical care is not reasonably accessible. It recognizes specified or documentably equivalent first-aid training.
Share the site address or access point, supervisor requirements and how crews rotate between sites.
Is this OSHA 10 or OSHA 30?
No. OSHA Outreach is a separate program and is not replaced by a first-aid card. Verify both items separately if your contract lists both.

Logging Crew First Aid & CPR
LOGGING / FORESTRY
Logging employees and supervisors who may work far from immediate medical care.
Ask us to check a proposed First Aid/CPR program against OSHA's logging Appendix B before relying on any card.
The federal logging standard requires each covered employee, including supervisors, to get current first-aid and CPR training meeting Appendix B.
Share crew roles, remoteness, transport plans and the exact written Appendix B expectation before booking.
Does a generic CPR card suffice?
No blanket claim is appropriate. Confirm the courses, practical components and paperwork required by your logging operation.

Utility Crew First Aid & CPR
UTILITY / ELECTRIC POWER
Electric power field crews, substations and utility supervisors planning responder coverage.
Request practical First Aid/CPR/AED training and identify the sites and job duties involved so the applicable rule can be checked.
OSHA 1910.269 adds first-aid coverage requirements for specified work on or associated with exposed lines or equipment energized at 50 volts or more.
Distinguish a fixed facility from a mobile crew, and tell us whether your work is construction or operations.
Does the course replace electrical rescue training?
No. Your employer still needs to establish the site-specific rescue, equipment and safety program.

First Aid & CPR for Confined-Space Teams
RESCUE TEAM / INDUSTRIAL
Designated emergency and rescue personnel at covered general-industry permit-required confined spaces.
Current first aid and CPR credentials may be one component of a broader rescue-team program; share the requirement before selecting a class.
OSHA 1910.146 requires first-aid and CPR training for designated rescue employees and a current certified member available. Other rescue competencies and practice are separate.
Send the name and scope of the applicable standard, plus the training and format your employer accepts.
Does this qualify a confined-space rescuer?
No. First Aid/CPR does not replace confined-space rescue evaluation, equipment instruction or practice.

Shipyards & vessel repair
Shipyard First Aid, CPR & AED
SHIPYARD / REPAIR
Shipyard employment teams covering multiple work areas and shifts.
Compare hands-on HSI and AHA First Aid/CPR/AED options with your employer's credential requirement; identify coverage gaps by shift.
Federal OSHA shipyard rules address staffing and response for each worksite and workshift, subject to stated exceptions. They address current first-aid and CPR certification for providers.
Plan for gate access, distance from vessels to the muster point and AED availability away from the main building.
Is this a merchant-mariner course?
Not necessarily. Workplace shipyard first aid and a Coast Guard credential course are separate decisions.

First Aid Training for Ports & Terminals
PORT / CARGO
Terminal and cargo-handling teams planning responder presence near loading, yard and waterside operations.
Ask about hands-on First Aid/CPR/AED for terminal staff and confirm the required first-aid certificate with your employer.
OSHA 1917.26 requires a valid first-aid certificate holder at covered terminals while work is in progress. Shipyard and longshoring rules have their own scope.

Does this include water rescue?
A first-aid card does not document lifesaving, water rescue or shipboard watch competence.

Merchant Mariner First Aid & CPR
USCG / MERCHANT MARINER
Applicants who need to distinguish the first aid and CPR entry for a Merchant Mariner Credential from STCW training.
Ask for the exact HSINST-203 format and verify 910CPR availability before paying. Some crews instead need employer-requested workplace First Aid/CPR.
The Coast Guard lists HSI HSINST-203 under applicable first-aid and CPR requirements for specified merchant mariner credentials; the listed course does not satisfy STCW endorsements.
Bring your NMC checklist or the exact credential name so we can distinguish it from STCW Basic Training.
Can I book any First Aid/CPR class?
Don't rely on the course headline alone. Verify the provider, approved delivery, course code and credential checklist first.

Childcare & preschool
Pediatric First Aid & CPR for Childcare
CHILDCARE / PRESCHOOL
Infant, toddler and preschool staff, directors and caregivers responsible for children in licensed centers.
Ask for a pediatric First Aid/CPR option and confirm the exact course and delivery format on NC DCDEE’s list. An adult First Aid class is not a substitute.

NC child care center rules cover First Aid and age-appropriate CPR. NC DCDEE lists HSI Pediatric First Aid/CPR/AED for applicable child and infant ages; the HSI Pediatric CPR AED or BLS listings address CPR only. Confirm delivery conditions and make sure the card identifies any required age modules.
Tell us the child age groups, whether staff escort children offsite and which written rule your licensing specialist provided.
Can I use an online-only course?
Do not assume it qualifies. NC center rules restrict distance learning for First Aid, and the approved-program listing distinguishes course formats.

K–12 / CAMPUS
Teachers, aides, coaches, campus staff and school teams with an emergency-response plan.
Discuss First Aid/CPR/AED for staff, pediatric scope for younger grades, and separate clinical BLS if the school requires it for medical staff.
NC graduation CPR instruction is a distinct student requirement; this staff training page does not establish eligibility for graduation or school employment.
Share the district's written credential and the AED locations in the gym, main office and outdoor areas.
Can teachers and school nurses take the same course?
Often their requirements differ. Send the district's role-specific wording before choosing a single course or two tracks.

Hands-On BLS for Dental Offices
DENTAL / CLINICAL
Dentists, dental hygienists, assistants and front-office staff with different training needs.
Discuss hands-on AHA BLS or another documented option that satisfies the applicable NC rule and practice requirements.
The NC dental board defines CPR certification by course content and manikin testing with the instructor physically in the room. Check the rule before relying on online-only training.
Share licensed staff roles, office sedation protocol if relevant, and whether nonclinical staff also need general First Aid/CPR/AED.
Can we complete it fully online?
Do not use an online-only class for the NC board’s physically present manikin-test requirement.

BLS, ACLS & PALS for Medical Offices
OUTPATIENT / CLINICAL
Outpatient practices, specialty clinics and clinical teams that need credentials without sending the whole team offsite.
AHA BLS is the clinical starting point when requested. Consider ACLS or PALS only for roles requiring adult or pediatric advanced life support.
Start with the employer, credentialing or clinic policy. A BLS course is not an ACLS, PALS or sedation credential.
List care roles and certification expirations, then identify staff who can train at the same time without closing patient services.
Can we combine clinical and nonclinical staff?
Plan separate tracks if the clinical staff need BLS but other employees need a First Aid/CPR/AED card.

Confirm whether the facility accepts a blended route, and whether learners have the right online component before arranging hands-on skills.
